verdicts.correction: The mode is implementor-defined only from 2023. Annex E.2 item 6 says: 'The mode of arithmetic used in evaluating compile-time arithmetic expressions and the handling of intermediate results is now explicitly implementor defined.' Its justification adds: 'The previous COBOL Standard required the use of an arithmetic mode that is no longer supported.' So at 2002 and 2014 the spec prescribed the mode, and COBOL.NET's documented System.Decimal choice (DOC-A.1-29) cannot set the expected output there. Under a prescribed wider-precision mode the lines differ. For example, 15E-28/2 = 7.5E-28 is exact in 32 or 34 digits, and GR3 truncation of 7.5 gives 'T2=   7.0', not 8.0. Likewise 9999999999999999999999999999*10 fits in 32 or 34 digits, so the negative's reject-at 2002 and 2014 is unfounded. Fix: move the positive golden to tests/conformance/2023/ and change the negative header to 'reject-at: 2023'. The CONFORMANCE.md row's '2002 onward' also contradicts E.2 item 6; that is an owner decision and a doc fix. The constructs.json row arithmetic-intermediate-precision-2023 already names this as an unconfirmed per-edition variant. The 2023 expected values themselves (D1 2, D2 100, D3 0, T1 2, T2 8, DEF-D1-IS-2, and the -ZZ9.9 layout) check out against the row.

SR9 only reserves the word IMP for the implementor and makes an IMP directive's syntax implementor-defined. Nothing in it requires '>>IMP SOMETHING' to be rejected; an implementation that defines IMP conforms and would accept it. The golden instead pins the generic 'unknown directive word is a syntax error' behavior. Its .err, COBOL0001, is the generic parse error ('unexpected >'), not a diagnostic for this rule. Any implementation that fails on any unrecognized >> line passes, whatever it does with IMP. The one enforceable part of SR9 is the reservation: IMP is not usable as a user or compilation-variable word, e.g. '>>DEFINE IMP AS 1' should be refused. That is untested, and the adjudicator charges it as an open defect under SR-7.3.3-7. Fix: move the row to not-closable, like GR-7.3.4-4, or re-point it to a reservation negative once that defect is fixed.

all_upheld_flag: Two of eleven were overturned. I ran cite.py --check on all 34 header citations and every one returned OK. The ONLY-golden header echoes cite.py's '5) 2. c)', which is the tool's OCR nesting. The real clause, per the rendered text order, is 5) c) 1. That is how the writer titles it, so the citation is right, but the echoed label is misleading. I re-derived every .out line from the source. For DOC-A.1-32 I checked each edited image by hand (9B9 gives '1 2', 909 gives '109', *99 of 5 gives '*05', 99CR/99DB of -12, +9.9E+99 of 15 gives '+1.5E+01' with E at position 5) and each ORD = code unit + 1. I recomputed the DOC-A.1-29 decimal results (2/3 = 0.666...67, times 3 truncates to 2; 100/7*7; the ties at 28 places). The -ZZ9.9, -9.9 and X(6) DISPLAY padding all check out. For discrimination: A2/A4 and HALF/NEG/MUL separate truncation from rounding and from floor; B4/B5 separate B-NOT and B-XOR precedence from left-to-right evaluation; the composite and surrogate programs would print LEN=1 and P2/P3=OTHER if a pair or sequence were treated as one position; each OO negative differs from its admitted twin in exactly the one feature the rule tests. I checked the TU-versus-TT and plain-group arms against rules 3 and 6, and only rule 7 is violated. I checked editions against constructs.json and the existing 2002 and 85 goldens (NX, B-XOR, TYPEDEF STRONG, IMPLEMENTS, ORD and ref-mod at 85). DOC-A.1-29 failed on Annex E.2 item 6. SR-7.3.3-9 failed because it only pins a generic parse error. Residual doubts I could not settle from the 2023 text, so I upheld: whether 2002 already had CONSTANT AS arithmetic-expression (constructs.json says it did, and the adjudicator flags a dossier gap); and whether pre-2023 compile-time arithmetic could change the CCE and constant goldens. It cannot: 7/2, 0.5+0.6 and 0.4*2 are exact or truncate the same way in any decimal or binary mode.
